artifacts.summary: Verifies the cross-repo source-store-collision counterexample (commits f49576632/4311617a2, tasks 398/399, four issue-log ids) and the mechanical gate blindness (orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh reads one repo's specs/state.json only; file-footprint-overlap.md's Non-Goals section has no cross-repo entry). Finds task 275's per-repo ruling reached [COMPLETED] without amendment, deferring the question to this record; finds two of 398/399's 'outstanding work' premises are now stale (a third, same-repo record-less channel (a) dispatch already repaired the index-entries.json leg). Frames the per-repo-vs-amend decision as a user_decision rather than deciding it; defers any Non-Goals text change and mechanism design to the plan phase pending the owner's answer.

user_decision.question: A measured incident (commit f49576632 editing agent-system/extensions/lean/** inside tasks 398/399's declared territory while both sat [NOT STARTED], from a BimodalLogic-repo dispatch with no visibility into this repo's task space) contradicts the premise behind task 275's ruling 'SCOPE -- RULED: PER-REPO... file_scope conflicts are inherently per-repo, so a global queue would carry no information the per-repo one lacks.' Task 275 has since completed implementing that ruling as written, explicitly declining to amend it and deferring this decision here. Should the per-repo scope ruling stand, or be amended to account for repositories sharing one source store?
options: A. Uphold the per-repo ruling as written. Document the cross-repo blind spot as an accepted, manually-detected risk in file-footprint-overlap.md's Non-Goals section. Build no new mechanism -- partly because the colliding actor in the measured incident carried no task record in either repo, so a mechanism keyed on task records or dependencies[] would not have prevented it anyway (confirmed again by a second, same-repo record-less dispatch that independently duplicated/pre-empted the same two tasks' work three days later).

B. Amend the ruling: file_scope conflicts are NOT inherently per-repo when multiple repositories share one source store. Direct a follow-up task to design a cross-repo visibility mechanism (e.g. a source-store-scoped lock or registry spanning both repos' task spaces) at plan time, with explicit treatment of the record-less-dispatch case this report shows recurring.

C. Amend narrowly: per-repo remains the default, but any repository whose .claude/ tree is deployed FROM a shared source store must register against that store's own lock/registry when editing it -- scoped only to the source-store-sharing relationship that actually collided, not a general cross-repo mechanism.
user_decision.recommended: A. Uphold the per-repo ruling as written. Document the cross-repo blind spot as an accepted, manually-detected risk in file-footprint-overlap.md's Non-Goals section. Build no new mechanism -- partly because the colliding actor in the measured incident carried no task record in either repo, so a mechanism keyed on task records or dependencies[] would not have prevented it anyway (confirmed again by a second, same-repo record-less dispatch that independently duplicated/pre-empted the same two tasks' work three days later).

memory_candidates.content: This repo's cross-task collision gates (orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh, file-footprint-overlap.md and every consumer wired to it) are scoped to exactly one repository's specs/state.json by construction (STATE_FILE=$PROJECT_ROOT/specs/state.json via common_repo_root). When a second repository's .claude/ tree is deployed from this repo's agent-system/** source store (per .claude-extensions.json's source_dir), that second repo's task space is architecturally invisible to every overlap/dependency check here, and vice versa -- two correctly-sited task records in two repos can claim the same source-store file with zero detectable collision. Separately, a channel (a) conclusion-stage dispatch carries no task record at all in either repo's terms, so even a hypothetical cross-repo mechanism keyed on task records would not see it; this has been measured occurring at least three times against the same two-task territory (agent-system/extensions/lean/** paths claimed by tasks 398/399) within one week.

When a task record is archived (/todo), its directory under specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/ is deleted entirely -- only a short digest survives in specs/CHANGE_LOG.md. A prior task's text that says 'if this ruling is amended, record the amendment as a dated note in this task record' becomes unfulfillable once that task is archived: the full plan/report/summary files are gone, retrievable only via git history (git show <archive-commit>^:<path>). Route such an amendment instead to whichever durable, non-task artifact now carries the ruling's substance (e.g. a context/pattern doc the implementation produced or updated).
